standard.title: Comprehension strategies for interpretation and evaluation
standard.description: use comprehension strategies such as visualising, predicting, connecting, summarising, monitoring, questioning and inferring to interpret and evaluate ideas in texts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use a range of comprehension strategies to construct meaning from texts and synthesise ideas across texts (AC9E7LY05). They have not yet applied these strategies specifically to interpretation and evaluation — using them to assess the credibility, effectiveness and significance of ideas in texts rather than merely to build comprehension.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students use comprehension strategies to interpret and evaluate ideas in texts, including assessing credibility and effectiveness of content.

nodes.label: Comprehension strategies for deeper reading
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply comprehension strategies (visualising, predicting, connecting, summarising, monitoring, questioning, inferring) purposefully to interpret ideas in texts — reading for what is implied and inferred, not only what is stated.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply at least two named comprehension strategies to a text and explain how they helped interpret ideas — specifically naming what the strategy surfaced about implied or inferred meaning.
nodes.typical_width: Apply a range of comprehension strategies purposefully to interpret ideas in texts; reflect on and connect information across and between texts; demonstrate inference and questioning as deliberate tools for interpretation.
wider: Apply comprehension strategies to a text from a cultural context unfamiliar to the reader — and reflect on which strategies worked, which were less effective, and what gaps in cultural knowledge affected comprehension
Use inferring and questioning strategies specifically to analyse what a text does NOT say — what is conspicuously absent from the text — and why
Compare how different comprehension strategies are required for reading a visual image vs a written text on the same subject

response_modes.reason: Comprehension strategies become truly useful when students have a full repertoire and can select the most appropriate strategy for a given reading challenge. Students who default to summarising need to experience questioning, inferring and monitoring as equally productive tools across different texts.

success_criteria: Names at least two comprehension strategies and explains how each was used with a specific text.
Demonstrates inference or questioning as a tool for interpretation — surfacing implied or unstated meaning.
nodes.hinge_reason: Node 2 requires applying comprehension strategies specifically to evaluation — assessing credibility and effectiveness. Students who only have summarising in their repertoire cannot apply inferring, questioning or monitoring to make evaluative judgements. The full strategy repertoire built at Node 1 is what Node 2 applies in a new evaluative mode.

nodes.label: Comprehension strategies for evaluation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use comprehension strategies to evaluate ideas in texts — assessing the credibility, effectiveness and significance of content, including evaluating the selection and composition of images for their effect on credibility.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply at least one comprehension strategy to evaluate an idea in a text — assessing whether it is credible, well-supported or effectively communicated.
nodes.typical_width: Use comprehension strategies to evaluate the content of texts, including determining criteria for evaluating website content, assessing the credibility of information and evaluating the selection and composition of images for their effect on the credibility or meaning of a text.
wider: Develop and apply explicit evaluation criteria for a class of texts (e.g. websites on a health topic) and use comprehension strategies to systematically evaluate multiple texts against those criteria

Investigate how the selection and framing of images in a news website affects reader credibility judgements — examining which images are selected, how they are cropped and what associations they trigger
Evaluate how cross-referencing information across texts (connecting strategy) can reveal inconsistencies or contradictions between sources — and what to do when reliable sources disagree

response_modes.reason: Evaluation requires applying criteria, not just responding with a gut reaction. The structured reasoning scaffold — what criteria am I using? what does the evidence show against those criteria? what is my evaluation? — needs to be made explicit before students can evaluate credibly rather than impressionistically.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Critical evaluation of online information, image credibility and cross-source consistency is high-value contemporary literacy territory. For advancing students, working with real-world media — news images, health websites, social media claims — provides rich, motivating and socially significant material.
success_criteria: Applies at least one comprehension strategy to evaluate an idea or image in a text.
States a clear evaluative judgement (credible/not credible, effective/not effective) with reasoning that references specific textual or visual evidence.
